_comment: Mama's Perspective — the property's open ground-truth questions, the kind only someone standing on the land can settle. Fetched at load by viewer.html (NOT inlined — no _DATA const, so check-data-inline.py does not track it; a failed fetch just means an absent queue, which is the correct calm behavior). This is a QUEUE, navigable and continuously populatable: Paul adds rows over time, refines them on what Mom engages with, and it is deliberately NOT one-and-done. Framing is Mom <-> app direct (her space to record her read of the place) — do NOT foreground Paul in prompts or acks. Mom's answers land via POST /api/feedback with context.{type:'mom-queue',questionId,kind}; Paul reads them with tools/read-mom-feedback.py, acts on the answer (edit plants.json, flip confidence inferred->verified), and sets the row active:false (or deletes it). Schema is forward-compatible: kind = confirm|react|open, answerMode = yesno|sentiment|text. v1 (2026-07-13) seeds confirm items + one standing open foot-line.

questions.prompt: You mentioned wanting the big categories across the top — **vehicles**, **equipment**, **house systems**, **gardening**, **wildlife**. Is that the whole list, or is something missing? Once we know, we can lay the app out so each one is easy to reach.
questions._note: IA card. ACTIVATED 2026-07-29 — Paul approved the wording and told it to the front ('move this card to the front, but keep a queue of cards'), so MAX_VISIBLE stays 5: he explicitly DECLINED the researcher's drop-to-1 recommendation. It leads the queue on file order alone. Origin: Mom told Paul IN PERSON (relayed 2026-07-29) that tabs across the top would appeal, naming vehicles / equipment / house systems / gardening / wildlife — her words, kept verbatim per CLAUDE.md 'adopt her words, never improve them'. Paul-relayed input is real input (channel doctrine, 2026-07-26). WHY THIS ASK AND NOT A BUILD: telemetry 2026-06-29..07-29 shows her device (d-szqlt0) fired card_expanded only 4x across 15 sessions — she reads the glance and rarely opens the second layer, which is where the radar, the by-day rainfall strip and the Almanac all live. Her tabs request is her own diagnosis of that. Paul's call 2026-07-29: reinforce the existing cards as doors FIRST, and ask her to confirm the category list so the reorganization is built on her answer rather than our guess. CLASS: preference/expertise — she is the sole authority on what she comes here for, so she cannot be wrong. This is deliberately NOT a verdict ask (1 answered of 35 offered on those). Seeded from HER last input, not from our uncertainty markers — harvest-questions.py could never have produced it. The 'no' path opens correctionPrompt so a category we never thought of can land. The purpose sentence is deliberate (Paul's ask): she is told what her answer will be used for. PLACED FIRST in file order — outstanding() slices the first 5 active confirms in file order (MAX_VISIBLE=5), so an appended card is never served. ⚠ Reflective: no _foldTarget, so it CANNOT self-clear and will hold the feedback watermark until retired by hand (active:false + resolvedAt), per the 2026-07-27 unprobeable rule.

questions.prompt: When you asked about looking back at what you'd written, you called it the journal — the app calls that card “The Almanac.” Would “Journal” fit better?
questions.resolution: Mom answered Yes 2026-07-29 8:54 AM ET — the card is now called "Journal". HANDLED THEN RETIRED, in that order: retiring first would have claimed we acted on a preference we hadn't. Rename scoped to the card alone (card-fieldnotes title + the two "Open Sync settings in the …" navigation strings that point AT it); the header tagline ("An Appalachian Almanac for 282 Church Mountain Road") and the ask-the-Almanac voice keep their name — the word carried three referents and she was asked about one. Retiring this also RELEASES THE FEEDBACK WATERMARK: as an unprobeable reflective card it held the ceiling, so every later answer of hers kept re-reading as new.
questions._note: Naming card. Wording approved by Paul 2026-07-28 and activated (authored content reaching Mom is human-confirmed; it was staged inactive until he said yes). Origin: she asked 'Is there a way to look back at these, eg in the journal?' (2026-07-26) and CLAUDE.md:56 says adopt her words, never improve them — so rather than renaming the card on her behalf, ask her. The 'no' path opens correctionPrompt so a third word of her own can land. ⚠ Reflective cards have no _foldTarget and therefore cannot self-clear: this one holds the feedback watermark until it is RETIRED by hand (active:false + resolvedAt), per the 2026-07-27 unprobeable rule. Placed FIRST among confirms 2026-07-28: outstanding() slices the first 5 confirms in file order (MAX_VISIBLE=5, viewer.html:9379), and appended it would have sat 6th and never been shown. It answers a question SHE asked, and it is reflective (answerable from a chair), so it outranks a weed that needs a walk outside. Displaces q-weed-stiltgrass below the cap until something ahead is answered or retired — the soft-cap's designed 'extras wait their turn'.

_ordering: ORDERED BY INFORMATION VALUE TO US (Paul, 2026-07-29) — not by area, not by age. outstanding() in viewer.html does .slice(0, MAX_VISIBLE=5) on THIS declaration order, so position is priority and position 6+ renders to nobody. Ranking axis, from the 2026-07-26 audit: an answer that unblocks a BUILD outranks one that fills a canon gap, which outranks a verdict on our own guess. Observation/expertise-class cards lead; verdict-class cards trail until the harvest template is reframed; preference cards last (no canon target, so no fold path and nothing to probe). q-weed-stiltgrass was 6th and therefore served to NOBODY for six days while carrying a photo Mom took — promoted to 2nd. q-strategy-pollinators takes its place out of view; verified unanswered first, so it cannot pin the feedback watermark the way q-almanac-name did.
